newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission had decided on DG XXIV's organisation chart. He said it had decided to move 117 civil servants from DGs III, V and VI. He also said that an additional 166 civil servants would be needed to complete the directorate general's task.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on the Court of Justice's judgments. He said the Court had judged that the right to obtain export refunds was lost if the boat carrying the goods happened to sink.

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan briefed on the Court of Justices' judgment in the field of equal opportunities. She said the Commission was very pleased the Court had ruled that a French ban on women working at night was discriminatory and therefore contrary to the 1976 directive on equal treatment and access to employment. She said Italy and France were the only member states to apply such a ban. Banning women from working at night can imply banning them from working at all or from obtaining higher salaries, she said.

Nolan also briefed on Friday and Saturday's informal Social Affairs Council. She said discussions would focus on coordination of the EU member states' employment policies. She said the ministers would discuss non-wage labour costs and the Renault closure.
In answer to a question, spokesman Willy Helin said the Commission had not been notified of a merger in the field of energy in Belgium.

Asked to react to the France/Germany stability agreement, spokesman Patrick Child said a reinforcement of the member states' economic cooperation was a good thing. He also said it had to be decided by the 15 member states and not between two member states only. Child also said the EU institutionnal balance had to be respected.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/205: Commission adopts strategy and two specific actions to combat acidification.
- IP/97/207: Commission adopts a pluriannual programme on the promotion of renewable energy sources - Altener II.
- IP/97/208: Social protection in the EU: modernisation and improvement.
- IP/97/211: The Commission proposes a common system for the taxation of energy products.
- IP/97/212: The Commission opens investigation into aid to Cordex, a Portuguese rope and cord manufacturer.
- IP/97/213: The Commission opens proceedings against financial measures in favour of Infraleuna GmbH, Sachsen-Anhalt.
- IP/97/214: The Commission authorises DM 70 million aid measures to Aircraft Services Lemwerder GmbH.
- IP/97/215: French "Plan Textile": statement by Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
- IP/97/216: Commission opens infrigement procedures against FF 20 billion for GAN restructuring.
- IP/97/217: The Commission approves aid to Vauxhall Motor Ltd in support of an investisment project in Ellesmere Port, Cheshire (UK).
- IP/97/218: The Commission opens a procedure concerning the possible misuse of shipbuilding development aid to Indonesia.
- IP/97/219: The Commission endorses South Africa's qualified membership of the Lome Convention.
- Speech/97/60: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson on the Fifth RTD framework programme.
- Speech/97/61: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson on "reinforce Europe's capacity to innovate".
- Eurostat news release No23/97: EU unemployment: 10.8% in January.
- ME97/13.3: Midday Express.
